newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil lowers monthly interest rate to 1.66 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil lowers monthly interest rate to 1.66 pct.

text.p: Brazil's Monetary Policy Committee lowered the Central Bank's basic monthly interest rate known as the TBC to 1.66 percent in February from 1.70 percent in January, confirming market expectations.
The committee, which informed markets of the new rate late Wednesday, also lowered its basic rate of assistance known as the TBAN to 1.84 percent from 1.88 percent.
The rates serve as a floor and ceiling for Central Bank rediscount lines. Banks that have drawn more than their authorized limit from rediscount lines are charged the hire TBAN rate.
The TBC and the TBAN are adjusted each month and market interest rates during the month roughly fluctuate between the two rates.
The four basis point cut in each rate was seen as a signal that the government did not think the economy was overheating, despite a widening trade gap.
